chunks: Aban ibn Uthman from Uqba that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, when the soul of a man reaches his chest, he sees. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what does he see?' He said, 'He sees the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of Allah says to him: I am the Messenger of Allah, receive glad tidings.' Then he sees Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and he says: I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, whom you used to love. Your love will benefit you today.
He said, I said to him, 'Can it be that one of the people sees this and then returns to the world?' He said, 'No. When he sees this, he dies forever, and that is a great thing.'

And that is in the Quran, the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who believed and were righteous. For them is good news in the life of the world and in the Hereafter; there is no changing the Words of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What does a believer see at the moment of death according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the visionary experience of a believer at the moment of death, where the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Imam Ali (AS) appear to offer glad tidings based on the believer's love for them. The Imam clarifies that this vision is not a temporary trance but a permanent state leading to death, linking it to the concept of 'Bashara' (good news) in the Hereafter. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt and the spiritual reality of the soul's transition.
